mn-sos-2026-kuhl-stennes-seth.name: Seth Kuhl-Stennes
mn-sos-2026-kuhl-stennes-seth.bio: Works for the Land Stewardship Project, with 20 years of experience in cooperatives, for-profit businesses and nonprofits.

positions.stance: Supports continuing paper ballots, early and absentee voting, and same-day registration, making Election Day a paid state holiday, and expanding voting rights regardless of citizenship or conviction.
Would facilitate cooperatives, credit unions and community land trusts and honor employers that pay living wages and support workers' right to unionize.
Supports eliminating the major/minor party distinction, a full public campaign finance system, and free and equal media access for all candidates.
Supports divesting state investments from weapons manufacturers, fossil fuels, nuclear power and similar companies and shifting them into entities upholding peace, human rights and ecological health.
Supports proportional representation for the Minnesota House, ranked choice voting for executive offices, and abolishing the Electoral College.

mn-sos-2026-tangen-george.name: George "Chip" Tangen
mn-sos-2026-tangen-george.bio: Lawyer and former legislative counsel to U.S. Rep. Jim Ramstad.

positions.stance: Says the state's chief elections officer "ought to be nonpartisan" and that Minnesota should elect secretaries of state unbound from the major parties.
Will spearhead reforms to eliminate barriers preventing independent and minor party candidates from appearing on the ballot; "Voters deserve more choices!"
Supports same-day registration and vouching, with those voters' ballots counted once their eligibility is confirmed: "Trust, but verify."

mn-aud-2026-reeves-jay.name: Jay Reeves
mn-aud-2026-reeves-jay.bio: Retired U.S. Army major and data analyst with private-sector financial reporting and business-analysis experience.

positions.stance: Would expand data analytics and continuous monitoring to flag unusual spending patterns earlier and more consistently.
Would move beyond static PDFs toward dashboards, trends, downloads and geospatial information showing how public money flows.
Would reduce duplicative manual reporting and use a risk-based approach to focus audit attention where it matters most.
Supports continuous monitoring, intrusion detection, encryption, staff training and strict access controls to protect public data.
Proposes legislation requiring new taxpayer-funded programs to be developed in collaboration with the independent auditing agency responsible for oversight.

ok-treas-2026-perry-kiefer.name: Kiefer Perry
ok-treas-2026-perry-kiefer.bio: Former Vice Chair of the Oklahoma Libertarian Party.

positions.stance: Will prohibit awarding state business as a reward for political loyalty or campaign contributions.
Would end low-interest loans to politically connected entities.
Promises "radical transparency" so every investment is made on market merit, not political favor.
Will explore sound money initiatives, diversifying reserves into tangible assets to guard against inflation.
Supports reducing state debt and resisting central intervention.

ok-labor-2026-hall-mike.name: Mike Hall
ok-labor-2026-hall-mike.bio: Career in engineering and project management, with some people-management roles.

positions.stance: Opposes state-mandated wage floors, saying wages are "a private contract between two consenting parties."
Proposes a strict review of state licensing, reserving mandatory licensure for high-risk professions and moving lower-risk occupations to voluntary certification.
Opposes reclassifying gig workers as employees and says benefits should be tied to the individual, not the employer.
Suggests considering private providers for routine boiler and elevator inspections and emphasizing consultation over fines.
Will keep Oklahoma a right-to-work state and advocates transparency so union members know where their dues are spent.

nv-sos-2026-barnhill-brad.name: Brad Lee Barnhill
nv-sos-2026-barnhill-brad.bio: Former systems analyst of twenty years and litigation paralegal of twenty years.

positions.stance: Would implement Question 7 voter ID through existing regulatory authority, ensuring Nevadans can actually get the ID they need.
Supports a flag-and-investigate approach to duplicate registrations, with questionable matches reviewed by a person before anything is touched.
Would require consistent election standards and training across all 17 counties.
Will push for regular, public-facing audit reporting on election administration.
Will use the office's voice to advocate repealing Nevada's Commerce Tax.

ar-sos-2026-pakko-michael.name: Michael Pakko
ar-sos-2026-pakko-michael.bio: Economist and member of the Governor's Council of Economic Advisors; State Chair of the Libertarian Party of Arkansas for the past decade.

positions.stance: Supports a nonpartisan redistricting commission using strictly non-political standards to draw legislative districts.
Says taxpayers should end support of party primary elections.
Says primary elections and filing deadlines are "way too early" and should allow candidates to file on a more appropriate timeline.
Supports reforming ballot-access rules for independent candidates, including early filing and narrow signature windows.
Supports adopting ranked-choice voting.

ks-sos-2026-morgan-scott.name: Scott E. Morgan
ks-sos-2026-morgan-scott.bio: Lawyer and former staff counsel to Sen. Bob Dole; co-founded a publishing company and is Executive Director of United Kansas.

positions.stance: Says confidence in elections is built through consistent rules, transparent administration, respect for local officials and "voters over party."
Does not support additional documentary citizenship requirements unless there is clear evidence existing safeguards are failing significantly.
Supports maintaining reasonable ID requirements while helping every eligible voter obtain a qualifying ID.
Is cautious about broad federal mandates that may override state and local election systems that are working.
Supports modern voting systems, cybersecurity and reliable audits; says "A paper ballot must remain the legal ballot of record."

ne-sos-2026-rumbaugh-paul.name: Paul Rumbaugh
ne-sos-2026-rumbaugh-paul.bio: Works in the Nebraska Fourth Judicial District Clerk of the District Court's Office, after 25 years in private-sector sales and operations.

positions.stance: Mission is to ensure every Nebraskan has "a voice that is heard and a vote that is counted," with transparency and accountability.
Will use every legal avenue to protect Nebraska's elections from federal interference or party leadership.
Supports ranked choice voting, saying "No one should be elected to office with less than 51% of the vote."

ne-sos-2026-krist-bob.name: Bob Krist
ne-sos-2026-krist-bob.bio: Retired U.S. Air Force lieutenant colonel and former Nebraska state senator for District 10.

positions.stance: Would administer elections impartially, "make it easy to vote legally and difficult to cheat," and certify honest results regardless of who wins.
Will demand transparency and accountability at every level of election administration.
Would keep strong, verifiable safeguards against fraud and abuse and verify each election that they work.
Will support county election officials with the resources and backing they need.
Would modernize the office to improve service to voters and businesses without compromising security.

sd-sos-2026-lesnar-tamara.name: Tamara J. Lesnar
sd-sos-2026-lesnar-tamara.bio: Former Compliance Officer at the Chicago Mercantile Exchange.

positions.stance: "I am committed to facilitating easier access to voting locations."
"I am dedicated to curbing double taxation."
Would develop a statewide database for ballot initiatives and signatures to streamline the process.
Would file lawsuits against laws that violate the Bill of Rights.

nd-spi-2026-bachmeier-levi.name: Levi Bachmeier
nd-spi-2026-bachmeier-levi.bio: Appointed North Dakota Superintendent of Public Instruction in October 2025; former teacher, coach, education policy adviser and school finance director.

positions.stance: Supports high standards and looking at academics, activities and real-world skills, not test scores alone.
Supports more instructional options while defending public schools, and more affordable dual-credit courses.
Says rewarding teachers means "smarter spending" not higher taxes, and the budget share for teacher pay should rise.
Says the Department of Public Instruction "should be a partner—not a barrier" to districts, educators and parents.

nd-spi-2026-foss-tracy.name: Tracy Layne Foss
nd-spi-2026-foss-tracy.bio: Teacher with over 30 years in education, including school district business manager and state CTE supervisor.

positions.stance: Says schools must fix root causes, "not just the symptoms."
Supports fully funding schools, including all legislative mandates.
Would listen to why teachers are leaving and support and respect them as professionals.
Says every child deserves access to healthy meals to reach their full potential.
Supports adequate funding and thoughtful implementation of the federal IDEA law.

dc-mayor-2026-hamilton-rhonda.name: Rhonda Hamilton
dc-mayor-2026-hamilton-rhonda.bio: Founder and Executive Director of the nonprofit M.I. Mother's Keeper and owner of Waterfront Insurance Network; former real estate broker.

positions.stance: Advocates a joint federal, state and local policy making it economically, socially and physically safe to live in all parts of the city.
Says "there must be a restoration, and maintenance of law and order before any program, no matter how well conceived, will succeed."
Proposes training opportunities and, with private industry, decentralizing expanding industry to provide employment outside overcrowded wards.
Advocates federal "assistance, but not control" for local governments.
Will sponsor a partnership with the private sector to restore job opportunities through programs economically attractive to industry.
Would build truly affordable housing, reform permitting timelines, and protect legacy residents and small businesses from displacement.
Would expand after-school programming, restore vocational pipelines and create partnerships for youth.
Would increase transparency across public safety agencies, expand mental-health interventions and restore community-police relationships.
Would streamline city services, modernize technology and simplify the resident experience.
Would support small businesses, protect consumers, promote local entrepreneurship and reform contracting to be fair and transparent.
Supports statehood for Washington, D.C., citing residents' lack of voting representation in Congress.
Supports housing as a human right, social housing, community land trusts and permanent housing for the homeless.
Supports municipalizing utilities and shifting to affordable electrification powered by renewable energy.
Supports "Free Metro Bus and Rail for all residents."
Supports a more equitable tax rate, a DC Public Bank, Initiative 82 and boosting TANF income support.

dc-atlarge-2026-silverman-elissa.name: Elissa Silverman
dc-atlarge-2026-silverman-elissa.bio: Former D.C. Councilmember (2015-2023), budget analyst at the D.C. Fiscal Policy Institute, and former journalist.

positions.stance: Will stop collaboration with ICE and ensure the Council defends D.C.'s right to self-determination.
Says the District's budget should deliver programs that work and taxpayers "should get their money's worth."
Co-authored the District's paid family and medical leave law and cites aid to businesses during COVID-19.
Advocates increasing housing supply by removing unnecessary obstacles to building and strategically using public lands and dollars.
Supports a properly trained and staffed police department and evidence-based programs to reduce gun violence.

wy-sos-2026-trujillo-tamara.name: Tamara Trujillo
wy-sos-2026-trujillo-tamara.bio: Worked 17 years in accounting and procurement at the Cheyenne refinery; earlier worked for Wyoming's Child Support Division.

positions.stance: Will streamline business filings, securities regulation and administrative processes to reduce red tape.
Will manage state trust lands and resources efficiently to maximize non-tax state income.
Supports cutting government waste and maximizing state revenues to eliminate private property taxes.
